overview: Sandhaven is South Shields' main beach: a long stretch of golden sand backed by dunes, with a promenade running the length of the seafront. It sits south of the Tyne piers and Littlehaven, so you look out across the river mouth towards Tynemouth from the northern end. It holds a Seaside Award, and The Sunday Times named it the UK's beach of the year in 2022.

It's very much a town beach. Behind the sand are Ocean Beach Pleasure Park, the Dunes and South Marine Park with its miniature steam railway, and the seafront has restaurants, cafés and pubs. In summer there are volleyball nets on the sand and regular events, from sandcastle competitions to music.

That makes Sandhaven a good choice when not everyone in your group wants to surf. South Shields Surf School runs surfing and paddleboarding lessons on the beach and hires out equipment, and the Metro gets you here from Newcastle without a car.

text: Sandhaven is a sandy beach break that faces the North Sea and needs swell from the north-east or east. Westerly winds blow offshore. The Tyne piers give the northern end a bit of shelter, which can make it smaller and cleaner when the open coast is messy.

On small summer days it's a gentle place to learn. South Tyneside Council points out that surfers and kayakers sometimes end up inside the beach safety zone, so if you're on a board, keep clear of swimmers and the flagged area.

South Shields doesn't work often. It needs a north-north-east swell and a south-westerly wind, and mid to high tide on the rise is best. The south pier gives shelter from a northerly wind. Water near the Tyne mouth can be affected by runoff, so be careful after rain. There's a car park above the beach.

cards.text: North Sea swell is most reliable outside summer; summer is often small but good for lessons.

practical.label: Lifeguards
practical.title: Two RNLI stations
practical.text: South Tyneside Council says there are two RNLI lifeguard stations on Sandhaven in the high season, usually May to September.

practical.label: Dogs
practical.title: 8am–6pm ban in summer
practical.text: Dogs are excluded from Sandhaven between 8am and 6pm from 1 May to 30 September. Outside those hours and dates, they're allowed.

practical.label: Getting there
practical.title: Sea Road, NE33 2LD
practical.text: The beach is on Sea Road. South Shields is the end of the Metro's Yellow line from Newcastle, and the Shields Ferry crosses to North Shields.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: Seafront
practical.text: A promenade along the whole seafront, plus restaurants, cafés and pubs. Volleyball nets go up in summer.

practical.label: Notice
practical.title: Plastic pellets
practical.text: After a vessel collision in the Tyne on 19 July 2026, pellets were reported on parts of the coast. Don't handle them, keep dogs on leads in affected areas and follow staff advice.

faqs.q: Is there a surf school in South Shields?
faqs.a: Yes, South Shields Surf School is based on Sandhaven Beach and teaches surfing and paddleboarding, with equipment hire.
Yes, two RNLI stations in the high season, usually May to September.

faqs.q: Can dogs go on Sandhaven Beach?
faqs.a: Not between 8am and 6pm from 1 May to 30 September. Outside those times they're allowed.
